manifestations.description: Persistent pain in his right ankle, disturbing his sleep for about 6 to 7 nights each month.
Pain increased by walking for 15 minutes; standing for 15 minutes; climbing stairs and slopes; squatting; change of weather.
Numbness around the scars over the right ankle.
Dorsiflexion of the right ankle reduced by 10� compared with the left (measurement of reduced range of motion).
Mild wasting of the right calf muscles (calf circumference difference of about 1 to 1.1 cm).
Unable to enjoy basketball, soccer, badminton or jogging which he used to enjoy before the accident.
Limited tolerance for prolonged standing or walking (earlier able to stand/walk 2 hours, later 45 minutes, later pain after ~15 minutes).

treatments_received: Immediate admission to Queen Mary Hospital on 8 June 1998 with immobilization and elevation
Operation on 15 June 1998 with internal fixation with plating of the fibula
Surgical removal of the implant on 6 September 1999
Rehabilitation including physiotherapy at Maclehose Medical Rehabilitation Centre
treatments_future: Glucosamine (prescribed for osteoarthritis) - future medication claimed

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He can no longer enjoy basketball, soccer, badminton or jogging which he used to enjoy before the accident.

Being confined to indoor duties in the report room does not provide the plaintiff with the same job satisfaction as operational and outdoor postings; he has been confined substantially to indoor duties since return to work.
Not suitable for jobs requiring prolonged standing, walking or physical activities; not fit for full constabulary outdoor duties such as running, chasing and apprehending suspects.
